summary: Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974), and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Shigenori Nagatomo taught Kin Cheung and Tao Jiang. He held posts at Temple University, where he is attested as a professor of religious studies in 1999 and attested in 2017.

Kamata studied Buddhist studies and sinology at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, also studying under Kodo Sawaki. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1988), Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1996), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1988–2001).
Working in religious studies and other fields, Shigeo Yokoyama studied at Kyoto University and held posts at Okayama University and Nara Women's University.

Specializing in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, Shigeru Gorai studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. His appointments included Kyoto Normal School, Koyasan University (~1957–1967), Otani University (1955–1978), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1964–1993).
Specializing in sinology and history/archaeology, Shigeru Kato studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from ~1920 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto studied in religious studies at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1963) and Harvard University (~1964–1967). He later held posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.
Specializing in sinology, Shih-Hsiang Chen studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1945–1971).
Working in linguistics and indology, Shikaripur N. Sridhar served as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026) at Stony Brook University.
Specializing in sinology and history/archaeology, Shikazo Mori studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later held a post at Bukkyo University (~1970–1978).

Working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology, Shili Xiong studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang (1920). He held posts at Boone University, Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1947–1948).

Working in indology, Shilpa Sumant was an Editor and Member of the Regulating Council at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and a member at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Futabatei studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. In linguistics and other fields, he held posts at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, Naval War College, Osaka Asahi Shimbun, and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun.
Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Shimin Geng studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1952) and later held a post there (~1953).

Working in indology and philosophy, Shin Fujinaga held an attested post at Hiroshima University (1992) and posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1991, and as Associate Professor in 2000).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono University (1919), Ryukoku University (1929), Kyoto University (1943–1953), and Kyoto City University of Arts (1953).

Specializing in religious studies and Buddhist studies, Shin'ichi Yoshinaga studied at Kyoto University. He founded the Kindai Pyramido Kyokai and held a professorship at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shin'ya Yasutomi studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held academic posts at Otani University (~1985–2010, 2014) and served as director at Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute and the Eastern Buddhist Society.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shindai Sekiguchi studied at Taisho University (~1928–1934). He later held professorships at Taisho University (~1950–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1986).

Working in Buddhist studies and indology, Shindo Kusumoto completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.
